paper.authors: Waisberg, I.; Klein, Y.; Katz, B.

publication_status.evidence: Crossref 10.33232/001c.138625 (api.crossref.org, checked 2026-10-14): The Open Journal of Astrophysics vol 8, 2025-05-27. Numbers transcribed from the arXiv v2 PDF (2025-05-25) and checked against it table by table.

source_of_data: ESO Phase 3 public GRAVITY products (SINGLE_SCI_VIS, not calibrated), ~/data/eso_binaries/trackb/zet_boo/oifits/; programmes 111.24UP.001, 111.264P.001, 113.26HF.001. Not an OiDB collection (see DATA_ATTRIBUTION.md, ESO Phase 3).
method: Single-field GRAVITY on the four ATs (K band, science channel, fringe tracker). The authors fit squared visibilities and closure phases with the interferometric binary model of Waisberg+2023 (Sect. 2.2). Free: K-band flux ratio and (dRA,dDec) per epoch. Angular diameters FIXED to 0.47 and 0.43 mas (isochrones). Errors: scatter between files/exposures: 40 microarcsec for GRAVITY epochs (formal errors far smaller). Closure phases of file averages very noisy (fringe tracker fibre hopping between near-equal components), so individual stable exposures (1-3 per file) were used.
flux_ratio_definition: f_B/f_A in per cent, K band; epoch average 88.3 +/- 1.9 %.
uncertainties: Formal fit errors are below 1 uas and the paper treats them as underestimated (data correlation, systematics). The adopted error is the scatter between the best fits of different files/exposures within an epoch: 40 uas per axis (Table 6 and Sect. 2.2). No per-epoch error ellipses are published. The paper does not mention the GRAVITY optical-aberration systematics (GRAVITY Collaboration 2021).

conventions.position: dRA, dDec = secondary B relative to primary A, east and north (as virgil's dra, ddec). PA north through east.
conventions.omega: Standard visual-orbit omega: the companion's relative to the primary, from the ascending node; the same star as virgil's omega, so no shift is applied. Checked: with this reading, crosscheck.orbits reproduces every published epoch position to better than 0.1 mas (tests/test_waisberg_references.py); the +180 deg reading is off by tens of mas.
conventions.degeneracy: Without radial velocities (Omega, omega) and (Omega + 180, omega + 180) give the same sky orbit; the paper reports the solution with Omega < 180 deg.
conventions.time: Tp is a decimal year; T_peri_mjd below = (Tp - 2000) * 365.25 + 51544.5 (Julian years), and P_day = P_yr * 365.25.

third_light: Very wide companion HIP 71759 (F0V) at 13.3 arcmin, far outside the field. Companions excluded: K flux ratio >1% at rho>~3 mas, >2% at 1-3 mas. No close companion detected.
notes: Companion inside a single AT fibre (all seps 57-88 mas, single-field mode; AT fibre FOV ~250 mas in K); NOT dual-field. Pericentre passage itself unobserved (target too close to the Sun); epoch 4 post-pericentre. Epoch 2 date printed 2023-06-14 in Table 1 (MJD 60110.06) but plot file named 2023-06-15. Near-equal brightness => 180 deg ambiguity resolved only by astrometric orbit (no phase referencing). Positions' absolute orientation relies on closure phases. Bandwidth smearing not discussed. Only 4 epochs; formal errors underestimated, 40 microarcsec scatter-based.

GRAVITY Collaboration 2021 (2021A&A...647A..59G, arXiv:2101.12098): static, field-dependent optical aberrations at fibre injection bias single-field binary astrometry (0.1-0.5 mas for S2 with the UTs in 2017-2018); dual-field pointings are not affected. These two single-field AT systems are the wide-separation cases that test whether such a bias shows in public AT data (design/gravity_aberration_test.md).
